statement: Exact cross-query sparse KV reuse with SCSD/common-private segmentation, no private-tail pruning, considering prefill and native verification rows
mechanism: Use same-request typed support intersection/union to reuse selected KV loads across query tokens while preserving each query support, multiplicity, causal mask and normalization
proposed_change: Evaluate QUILT exact cascades or pinned FlashInfer union-mask preparation as implementation options under existing AT02. In native verification, share typed compressed-cache common entries first; keep SWA private. Never assume five target query rows.

support.quote: This push-down is exact and trades a small amount of sharing for improved tile utilization.

counterevidence: Target prefill already gathers and dequantizes BF16 once; donor per-query dequantization savings cannot be claimed there.
Ascend NPU Top-2048 results do not predict B200 Top-512 performance.
Packing, masks, padded tiles, sorting and query/head layout costs remain unknown.
The existing fused core reuses KV across 64 heads of one token; L2 may already supply incidental cross-token reuse.
Per-row Q and Top-K are not guaranteed equal at compression ratio 2; short-context all-candidate filling is a separate exception.
pin_check: Source baseline only; configured FlashMLA dependency pin is not live-binary attestation.
prior_comparison: Same AT02 bounded query grouping and reuse mechanism. This adds concrete algorithm and donor options plus a native-verification exposure question; it is not a new identity.
evaluation_plan: First inspect archived typed index traces for overlap and existing kernel shapes. Later, if authorized and eligible, compare token/logit correctness and per-round timing before unchanged agent-75 and Mooncake tests. Separate prefill TTFT and decode ITL arms.
ROI: Unknown: no compatible target overlap or exposed-time measurements.

statement: Capacity-preserving context-work-aware membership of already-enabled uniform-decode microbatches
mechanism: Equal scheduled query-token counts can conceal unequal context-dependent producer-indexer work. Permute eligible complete request bundles into equal-capacity microbatches while preserving DP-agreed splits.
proposed_change: After auditing actual DBO and adaptive-verification eligibility, evaluate a capacity-constrained context-work partition before request-derived metadata is built. Retain the original when the proxy worsens. Preserve request, cache, draft, logit and inverse-output mappings and class ordering. Never change rank-local split points independently.

support.quote: It moves no data between KARAT devices
Splitting at the midpoint of the DP-padded token count

Microbatching pads every

counterevidence: DBO defaults to false; actual activation is unknown.
Adaptive verification reallocates draft budgets on GPU and can invalidate CPU bundle sizes.
Uniform query length with an odd request count can straddle the midpoint.
Per-microbatch DP token equality is a collective contract.
The greedy proxy worsened in 2 of 200 synthetic cases.
A local work-proxy reduction does not establish distributed critical-path improvement.
pin_check: V2 slice helper and DP metadata verified at c455; actual launch is not live-attested.
prior_comparison: Root searched 133 prior cards and found no exact context-weighted membership intervention. This differs from DP agreement RUNTIME-R2-02, SM quota N03 and route-histogram tile selection M01.
evaluation_plan: Audit saved launch flags and complete uniform-bundle exposure. Replay actual CPU batch metadata and inverse mappings first. Later, unchanged agent-75 and Mooncake tests should stratify mixed-context traffic, retain the same DBO baseline, and report acceptance, ITL, TTFT tails and all-rank exposure. No GPU work now.
ROI: Unknown. Scoped exposure is zero if DBO is off or no eligible batches occur.
